title: Fantasy football Week 1 takeaways: Josh Allen rolls while other top QBs struggle
content:
Considering the quality of the Houston Texans defense, this was arguably the best game Josh Allen has ever played. He’s such a fantasy dynamo. He had a four-touchdown day, two via the ground (one on a 21-yard dash). He also threw for 334 yards, at a clip of 11.5 yards per attempt. He now has 81 career rushing TDs. His 51 games with a rushing and passing TD is an NFL record.

The Dalton Kincaid brigade is lighting up stogies. Enjoy, my friends. More important than the 130 receiving yards, perhaps, were the 73 percent snaps. I felt his limits as an inline blocker would continue to limit his opportunities on a team that prioritizes the run. James Cook had a bad day, so maybe that’s the price you pay. I personally would gladly pay it, but I live for the passing game. The Buffalo Bills haven’t been willing to. Will this be the plan against a normal opponent? It’s too soon to know. But why would Buffalo change anything?

The Los Angeles Chargers are in midseason form when it comes to “Chargering.” I’m shocked by how thoroughly they were dominated by the Arizona Cardinals. Mike McDaniel had about as bad a day as you can have as a new offensive coordinator, given the perception of the talent on this roster.

We’re on Ladd McConkey alert, as he exited late in the third quarter with what is being called a “chest” injury. If it ends up being broken ribs, that would probably be a multi-week absence. David Njoku — who had three of his five catches and 40 of 58 receiving yards in the fourth quarter after McConkey was out — is definitely rosterable. I can’t abide by going 5 feet out of your way to play Justin Herbert in one-QB leagues until he shows the form we expected and that he has adapted to his new offense. This offense was designed for a QB with a weak arm. Is this a round hole for a square peg?

Arizona’s Trey McBride is money in the bank (9/95/1), but it was a bad day for Marvin Harrison backers, as he was targeted just three times, catching one pass for 33 yards.

Neither offense looked good in the Washington Commanders’ matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, though Commanders rookie receiver Antonio Williams caught my eye. It was a rough day for Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin managers. God help you if you stacked them. In one big league, I picked Caleb Williams over Daniels because the Commanders just scared me and who knows who the real Daniels is. I like the early returns. I ended up dropping Daniels well below industry consensus in my final preseason rankings, but it was still way too high.

The Eagles’ offense was basically Jalen Hurts to Dallas Goedert. There were flashes from Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, but nothing to get you too excited.

This was the day we wanted from the unleashed Green Bay Packers passing game. But they couldn’t hold a lead against a backup QB because they have no running game without Jacobs. I did not envision Matthew Golden leading the Packers in targets (12). You should start Golden in Week 2 if you play in a league that is even remotely deep.

The Minnesota Vikings lost Kyler Murray early, and he’s in danger of missing multiple weeks given the symptoms he exhibited of a severe concussion. Backup Carson Wentz executed the plan of throwing the ball to Justin Jefferson, who had his best game since Sam Darnold left town.

The Las Vegas Raiders–Miami Dolphins game looked like a battle of running backs, but Ashton Jeanty pantsed De’Von Achane. Jeanty followed up his five receiving TDs of 2025 with two more in Week 1 — I didn’t think the five from last year would be remotely predictive. The takeaway from Miami is that rookie Caleb Douglas (5-94) looks like the WR to get in Miami.

My theory of the case with Caleb Williams is that there was untapped running value here. He tied for second last year among all players with the most runs over 20 mph, according to Next Gen Stats. But he’s been mostly a play extender and not a runner. Sunday, he was a true multi-threat player with 65 rushing yards and a pair of TD runs, both from distance and displaying his elite speed.

Williams also makes some of the most incredible throws so routinely. The TD pass to Cole Kmet should be hanging in the Louvre. I can’t explain Colston Loveland being shut out. I will reiterate, though, that if a team has the desire to sell out and stop a tight end, it can. D’Andre Swift (18/124/3) is a low-end RB1. Kyle Monangai (10/100/1) is someone you have to roster.

I followed the money with Kenneth Gainwell, and that was a bust that’s not likely to change without a change to Bucky Irving’s health. But I also followed it with Jalen Coker, and that looks like a hit. Every season, a player from the bottom of the WR queue becomes a top-12 WR, and Coker looks like that guy. He has more than 130 receiving yards with eight-plus catches and a TD in each of his past two games (including last year’s postseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams). I think Tetairoa McMillan is a weak No. 1, so Coker could practically match him in targets.

Bryce Young was very good. I wouldn’t play him in one-QB leagues, but he’s not a reason to keep any Carolina Panthers player on my bench, either.

Irving won the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ starting RB job. This is a loss for me and following the money. It’s also a loss for the Bucs’ ownership. I’d fire my GM if he just threw $10 million away for a running back he clearly has no vision for. We expect teams to communicate intent with their money and draft picks. In other words, to act rationally. As of now, you can’t play Gainwell, and Irving is a solid RB2. I mean, the Bucs have Gainwell returning kickoffs — busy work.

Baker Mayfield is a whirling dervish on the field. He has to calm down and play under more control. The Bucs’ offense was so unimpressive, but he managed to mask that with points, some generated by their defense. Finishing with fewer than 300 yards against the Cincinnati Bengals is a bad offensive game.

What is wrong with Burrow? He does not make plays anymore. You can’t have Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combine for five catches and 71 yards. If that happened to Dak Prescott with his receivers, we’d send him to jail. And as I’ve noted here before, Burrow has been below average to average in yards per pass attempt for three years running. I am not saying he’s not good, but you should be concerned about him and, by extension, his receivers.

The Texans offense was about as expected. There was more David Montgomery action — 23 touches, three TDs — than I projected, but this was more a descriptive game than a predictive one, given he averaged 3.0 yards per tote. At age 29, I can’t see Montgomery being a bell cow or having remotely viable efficiency. If you can get second-round value, you should trade Montgomery right now. And that’s possible.

What a strange game in Detroit. Jahmyr Gibbs delivered. So did Amon-Ra St. Brown. But overall, the Lions’ passing game was abysmal (5.1 yards per pass play).

On the other side of the ball, the New Orleans Saints did nothing, and I was crafting apologies for being bullish on their players, and especially Juwan Johnson. Tyler Shough was awful for most of the game. But a switch seemed to go off after a long pass to Chris Olave, who is great. And Shough ended up throwing for 410 yards and three touchdowns. Olave caught 10 passes for 182 yards. And Johnson made three game-changing catches in the final minutes and overtime after inexplicably being completely ignored for most of the contest.

I would make a waiver bid on Devaughn Vele, who made a great diving catch to get the Saints back into the game. I’ll have more on that in my weekly Market Share Report, which will be posted a little later on Tuesdays than in previous seasons (more on that below).

The only comment I have on the Atlanta Falcons (at the Pittsburgh Steelers) is that Bijan Robinson is so great that nothing can slow him. The rest of the offense needs a QB to step up, but it’s not going to be Cooper Rush, who is strictly a game manager. He did miss Kyle Pitts on an underthrow early that probably would have been a long TD. Let the QB situation play out until you get one of the two players we thought we were getting. The Atlanta QB position is like Spinal Tap drummers right now.

The New York Jets–Tennessee Titans matchup went according to expectations. I thought the Jets would have an average-ish offense and the Titans would be unplayable except for Wan’Dale Robinson. I wouldn’t be banging the table for Robinson right now, either, but he’s at least rosterable.

Speaking of the Jets, they have the Indianapolis Colts’ first-round pick next year, and Indy looks bad. The Jets also have the better of the 2027 first-round picks for Green Bay and the Dallas Cowboys. I would bet right now that the Jets finish with a better record than one of those teams.

Maybe the Baltimore Ravens are great and Lamar Jackson is going to challenge for the MVP. He played like an MVP on Sunday. But Zay Flowers (5/150/1 in just the first half) is so integral, and he aggravated his summer hamstring injury, so I fear he’ll be out for weeks. Derrick Henry is a player I just can’t project because he violates all the rules, but we can’t expect him to keep running like this forever, can we? Maybe John Riggins is the only back in his 30s who remained a top runner, but Riggins was nowhere near as efficient as Henry (24/144/3).

Daniel Jones looks like a guy who blew out his Achilles tendon last year.

My note for the Cleveland Browns–Jacksonville Jaguars matchup is that I’ve fantasized about leagues where you don’t draft defenses; rather, you draft an offense and get what each defense it plays scores against it. If that was the rule in a league, the Browns would be worth drafting in the fourth or fifth round. I’m dead serious. That’s 10 to 20 points per week.

Bhayshul Tuten decisively won the first round in the battle for Jacksonville’s RB job, for which he and Chris Rodriguez Jr. were listed as co-starters.

It’s early, but I don’t think Brian Thomas Jr. is going to work out. Something is just off. Despite the draft capital and rookie success, this is clearly now Parker Washington’s show (5/83/1).
